notes: Found via the header mega-nav: a single link distinctly styled (text-danger / red) reading 'Clearance', hrefing to /sale - this is the site's own permanent nav label, not a generic 'Sale'/'Offers' campaign link. Opening https://www.foslighting.in/sale confirms: page <h1> is literally 'Clearance'; product cards on the homepage carousel that link into /sale/... PDPs carry an on-page badge reading 'Clearance Sale' (plus a percent-off chip, e.g. '60% Off') rather than a temporary-campaign label like 'Diwali Sale' or 'Black Friday'; the backend product tag field 'websiteCategories' for these same products is literally 'sale', a standing catalogue tag (not a date-bound promo flag). This satisfies the brief's Clearance-vs-Sale test: the site's own taxonomy (nav label, page heading, product badge) treats this consistently as Clearance/permanent-markdown merchandising, not a seasonal or percent-off campaign page, so it was NOT downgraded to an ambiguous flag. Checked sitemap.xml and nav/footer for other clearance-style terms (Outlet, Final Sale, Last Chance, End of Line, Discontinued) - none found; /sale is the only such listing. qty=142 cross-verified three ways on the same fetch: the page header count ('142 products'), the pagination footer text ('Showing 20 of 142 products'), and the embedded pagination JSON object ({"currentPage":0,"pageCount":8,"total":142,"limit":20}) - all three agree, so treated as the site's own exact total, not a capped/rounded widget. Single undifferentiated listing - no genuine sub-categories (the facet filters on the page, e.g. Ceiling/Table/Floor, are query-string facets over this same /sale index with their own counts, not separate Clearance child listings, consistent with the facet-vs-taxonomy distinction already documented for this company in the prior Home-Decor pass).
